_about: Every public-domain Adolph Saphir (1831-1891) text the Word Hoard holds: the Hebrew Christian expositor, born at Pesth, Presbyterian minister in London. Not Moritz Gottlieb Saphir (humorist), not Jacob Saphir (traveller), not Philipp Saphir, not Elijah or Marie Saphir. All Internet Archive OCR, raw; no CCEL or Gutenberg Saphir exists (checked 2026-10-02). Posthumous printings before 1931 are PD and marked.

saphir-hebrews-1: Expository Lectures on the Epistle to the Hebrews, first series, ch. 1-7 (1875 printing)
saphir-hebrews-2: Expository Lectures on the Epistle to the Hebrews, second series, ch. 8-13 (1874)
saphir-christ-and-the-church: Christ and the Church: Sermons on the Apostolic Commission (1874)
saphir-hidden-life: The Hidden Life: Thoughts on Communion with God (1877)
saphir-divine-unity: The Divine Unity of Scripture (1892, posthumous)
saphir-christ-and-israel: Christ and Israel: Lectures and Addresses on the Jews (ed. David Baron, 1911, posthumous)
saphir-tr-auberlen-daniel: K. A. Auberlen, The Prophecies of Daniel and the Revelation of St. John, translated by Adolph Saphir (1856)
saphir-memoir-carlyle: Gavin Carlyle, 'Mighty in the Scriptures': A Memoir of Adolph Saphir (1893); about Saphir, not by him
